title: Label Partitions
statement:
Cut a lowercase string into as many consecutive pieces as possible so that no letter shows up in more than one piece, and report the piece lengths.

Contract
- `text` is non-null and contains only the letters `a` to `z`; it may be empty.
- Every letter that occurs in `text` must lie entirely inside one piece, and the pieces, read in order, must rebuild `text`.
- Return the lengths of the pieces from left to right, using as many pieces as possible. The result is therefore unique.
- An empty `text` has no pieces, so the result is an empty list.

Examples
- `partitionSizes("abcabdxyx")` returns `[5, 1, 3]`: the pieces are `abcab`, `d` and `xyx`.
- `partitionSizes("zzzz")` returns `[4]` because a single letter cannot be split apart.
- `partitionSizes("qrst")` returns `[1, 1, 1, 1]`.
hints: A piece must reach at least as far as the last occurrence of every letter it contains.
Record the last index of each letter first. Then sweep left to right, keeping the furthest last-index seen in the current piece; when the sweep index reaches it, the piece can close.

Closing a piece exactly when the index equals the running furthest end makes every piece as short as possible. Intended complexity: O(n) time for a string of length n and O(1) extra space, since the table has 26 entries and the list holds at most 26 pieces.
inputSyntax: Input: a lowercase string, for example: abcabdxyx
